todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.
outcome: Make explicit custom-group removal durably clear only the conversation follows invalidated by that departure, including manual and root/reply auto-follows, while preserving independently valid follows and ensuring delayed or replayed cleanup cannot erase a follow established after a genuine re-add.
scope: Extend the existing `Memba.Membership.Policies.ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows` collaboration; the accepted `Membership.remove_custom_group_member/2` path already emits the reusable `GroupMemberRemoved` fact, so do not create a second cleanup process.

Give the public explicit-removal use case a completion contract that does not report success before its required Messaging cleanup is durable, while preserving its existing Commanded return modes and task-001 authorization/event semantics.

Clear every current follow source through public Messaging commands and idempotent facts: a true manual `ConversationFollowed`, a root sender auto-followed by `MessageSent`, and a reply author whose auto-follow currently exists in the projection even though the reply event lives outside the root conversation stream.

Implement and test an ordering or generation/version mechanism so remove, rapid genuine re-add, and explicit follow-again are causally safe; repeated or replayed delivery of the old removal must be a no-op against the newer follow.

Keep cleanup scoped to follows actually invalidated by the removed group. Preserve a follow for a different conversation in another group and preserve a shared-conversation follow when the person still has effective read access through another active group.

Retain the origin-replaying handler's durable behavior and avoid falsely completing cleanup from an empty lagging conversation-access projection when that would allow an old follow to survive and later resume.
Keep Everyone/Admin handling unchanged: explicit custom-group removal still rejects system groups, and synthetic or replayed system-group removal facts do not clear conversation follows.

Add focused aggregate/integration tests that directly prove cleanup completion, all follow origins, duplicate/replay idempotency, rapid remove/re-add/follow safety, unrelated/shared access preservation, projection-lag behavior, and system-group no-ops.
scope_exclusions: Do not change the accepted Club authorization, actor/target validation, self/last-member rules, role preservation, or `GroupMemberRemoved`-only Membership decision except for the application-service cleanup completion needed by this packet.
Do not implement the broader query/action/provider-handoff authorization work, queued-delivery cancellation, or open-LiveView refresh assigned to pending tasks 009-011.
Do not add Leave/Remove controls, confirmations, member-row changes, former-member surfaces, or empty-group UI behavior assigned to tasks 012-014.
Do not edit the iteration-064 acceptance feature files or implement the browser/domain acceptance layer assigned to tasks 015-016.
Do not redesign unrelated Messaging delivery or multi-group conversation editing behavior.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 017 and the deterministic `dev_check` node own the final repository gate.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 2 and the acceptance/open-technical-decision text require public Messaging APIs, idempotent unfollow facts, root/reply auto-follow cleanup, stale remove/re-add safety, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behavior.

Iteration 062 introduced the origin-replaying Membership-to-Messaging cleanup collaboration and its club-departure completion ordering; iteration 064 must extend that boundary rather than add another process.
Membership owns group membership while Messaging owns follow state; coordinate through public context APIs rather than direct cross-context projection writes.
The Club stream remains the authoritative membership lifecycle and identity boundary; system-group facts remain separately policy-maintained consequences.

The existing strong handler starts from origin, filters custom `GroupMemberRemoved` facts, lists conversations through Messaging, and dispatches public unfollow commands with follow-projector consistency.

`remove_custom_group_member/2` currently performs a plain dispatch, while club-member lifecycle dispatch augments consistency with `ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows`; `add_custom_group_member/2` also needs to participate in whichever stale-cleanup ordering contract is selected.
The accepted 062 club-rejoin mechanism waits for durable cleanup progress before projecting `ClubMemberAdded`; use it as ordering precedent without coupling independent projection rebuilds.

Public `list_conversations_for_group/1`, `follow_conversation/2`, `unfollow_conversation/2`, and effective conversation-access APIs are the current cross-context seams. The private email-token reconciliation demonstrates the existing projection/write-model mismatch for auto-follow before unfollow.
The root-routed aggregate makes manual follow/unfollow idempotent and rehydrates root `MessageSent`, but it cannot see an auto-following reply `MessageSent` stored on a separate reply stream.
The projection records both root and reply `MessageSent` auto-follows plus explicit follow/unfollow facts in one deterministic conversation/person row.

Existing tests cover handler shape, origin replay, club-departure cleanup, suspended-handler club rejoin ordering, no automatic follow restoration, and easy duplicate idempotency; they do not yet cover explicit group removal, reply-only auto-follow, post-re-add follow replay safety, shared access, or direct system-group no-ops.
Existing focused coverage establishes projected manual state and root/reply `MessageSent` auto-follow behavior.
Existing tests establish that effective access composes across multiple group grants; cleanup must not destroy a global conversation/person follow while another active group still supplies access.
The existing lagging-access-projector regression proves authoritative delivery denial but currently permits cleanup to miss the conversation and leave an old follow behind.
Use focused tests, `start_supervised!/1` for test processes, monitors or synchronization primitives instead of sleeps, and deterministic process synchronization for race coverage.

constraints: Use the accepted actor-bearing custom-group removal and existing `GroupMemberRemoved` fact; do not introduce a parallel member-removal command or route through club/role removal.
Keep cross-context writes behind public Messaging APIs and event-sourced commands/facts; do not delete or toggle Messaging projection rows directly from Membership code.
A reply-author auto-follow must become authoritatively unfollowable even though its `MessageSent` event is stored on the reply stream; a projection-only false value is not sufficient.
Stale-cleanup safety must cover the actual remove/re-add/follow race and origin replay, not only repeated cleanup while already unfollowed.
The follow is conversation/person scoped, not group scoped. Do not unfollow a shared conversation when another active group still grants that person effective read access.

Preserve historical event replay. If command/event fields or generation identity change, old `MessageSent`, follow, unfollow, and Membership facts must remain readable with their established semantics.
Preserve `ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows` durable origin replay and Membership projection rebuild independence; do not make ordinary projection reset replay external side effects.
Preserve explicit-removal return values, caller-selected Commanded returning modes, and exact-retry behavior while adding required consistency.
Limit edits to the cleanup/follow/order seam and its focused tests; leave pending authorization, delivery, LiveView, UI, acceptance-runner, and final-gate obligations untouched.
completion_evidence_required: List changed paths and identify the selected completion-ordering or generation/version mechanism, including why an old cleanup cannot erase a newer post-re-add follow.
Report exit statuses and test counts for both focused test commands on the exact handoff state, plus `git diff --check`.
Identify tests proving explicit `remove_custom_group_member/2` does not complete before required follow cleanup and that its accepted Membership event/return contract remains intact.
Identify emitted Messaging facts proving cleanup of a true manual follow, root-sender auto-follow, and reply-author auto-follow, including idempotent duplicate/replayed removal behavior.
Show a remove/re-add/follow race or controlled delayed-handler test where the genuinely new follow survives late old work while the pre-removal follow does not resume automatically.
Show that a different-group conversation follow and a shared-conversation follow with surviving effective access are preserved, while Everyone/Admin cleanup facts remain no-ops.

Show that conversation-access projection lag cannot falsely acknowledge cleanup and later reactivate a pre-removal follow. If this cannot be solved within the bounded seam, return a concrete replan instead of weakening the obligation.

latest_review.summary: Task 001 is accepted: the actor-bearing public removal path is Club-routed, emits only the reusable `GroupMemberRemoved` fact for a transition, preserves club roles/membership, and rejects system groups.

latest_worker_result.summary: The accepted predecessor reported focused Membership suites passing with no unresolved gaps; this packet begins at the follow-cleanup consequence of its committed `GroupMemberRemoved` fact.
